name: Hydra–Centaurus Supercluster
tagline: The supercluster adjacent to Virgo — a double lobed gathering that includes the Great Attractor region.

facts.label: Notable
facts.value: Hosts the Great Attractor mass concentration

facts.label: Role
facts.value: Pulling the Local Group toward the supergalactic centre

history: The Hydra–Centaurus Supercluster is the massive neighbouring structure in the supergalactic plane toward Centaurus — two lobes of cluster density separated by a filament gap. It contains or sits near the Great Attractor, the gravitational anomaly pulling the Local Group and everything around it at ~600 km/s. Its X-ray-bright clusters and rich galaxies make it one of the heaviest concentrations of nearby matter we can map.
